Hi Aisha,

Thanks — we can provide both architecture artifacts and a short log sample. Quick summary up front: Redwood Dedicated uses tenant-attached GPU pools (we do not place arbitrary customer workloads together on the same GPU instance unless the customer has explicitly chosen a shared-tenant offering). For customers on Dedicated capacity we offer two modes: (1) physical GPU reservation per tenant (node pinned) and (2) partitioned GPUs using MIG where supported; both modes include kernel-level isolation plus our runtime namespacing for KV caches.

I'm looping in Jonas (runtime/security) and Ben (account lead) to deliver the artifacts and answer any remaining SIG specifics. We'll attach a short isolation overview and a SIG responses spreadsheet once we validate the sample logs.

Hi all — attaching a short technical note (redwood_isolation_overview_v2.pdf) and a sanitized sample log (kvnamespace-eviction-sample.log) that demonstrates:

- GPU assignment model: for Dedicated customers we either: (A) pin an entire host/GPU set to the tenant (no other customers scheduled), or (B) configure NVIDIA MIG slices with explicit tenant-to-MIG mappings.
- Kernel/process isolation: containerd + seccomp profiles scoped per-tenant; we also mount per-tenant cgroups and use hardware-level isolation where available (MIG slice boundaries).
- KV cache namespacing: runtime assigns each tenant a UUID-prefixed namespace; the KV store enforces tenant checks on GET/SET/DEL and enforces an ownership header validated by the runtime before access.
- Eviction behavior: eviction is LRU per-namespace and evictions are only triggered against objects within the same namespace. The provided sample shows a control trace where tenant A's RX push caused local LRU in namespace A, and no cross-namespace eviction occurred.

Sanitization notes: logs scrubbed for tenant IDs and IP addresses; we can provide redacted but verifiable artifacts under an NDA if needed.

Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Runtime Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_isolation_overview_v2.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB), kvnamespace-eviction-sample.log (text, 12KB)

If it's runtime-enforced, do you have any design notes on hardening and periodic integrity checks?

Also procurement may ask for a signed letter confirming the Dedicated offering will be single-tenant at the GPU instance level if they commit node reservation.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: dedicated GPU co-residency + KV cache scope

Aisha — short answers inline and attached a filled SIG spreadsheet.

1) MIG reconciliation: We maintain an allocation ledger in our orchestration control plane (document link attached). During host maintenance we mark affected MIG slices as "quarantined" and perform a controlled reprovisioning: tenants with node reservations are scheduled onto available reserved hosts; automated reassignment to a different tenant does not occur unless the customer has opted into a "rapid-recovery shared pool" (explicit opt-in). I've attached the orchestration runbook excerpt in the Drive folder.

2) KV namespace enforcement: Enforcement is performed by an independent access-control module within the runtime process boundary — the module is implemented as a minimal, auditable service with strict memory and syscall restrictions. We also run periodic integrity checks that verify namespace mapping tables against a signed ledger in the control plane; any discrepancy triggers an alert and automatic isolation of the affected runtime. We described the hardening checklist in the attached SIG spreadsheet (sig-responses-QuantifyAI-20261105.xlsx).

3) Procurement letter: Ben — can you send the signed single-tenant confirmation letter once procurement is ready?

Attached: sig-responses-QuantifyAI-20261105.xlsx (SIG answers + references), redwood_isolation_overview_v2.pdf, kvnamespace-eviction-sample.log

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week to walk the security team through the artifacts.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim

Redwood Inference
